entry.title: Proximity Transient Absorption in van der Waals Heterostructures
entry.summary:
Transient absorption spectroscopy is a widely used technique for investigating ultrafast electronic dynamics, where transient optical signals are generally interpreted as arising from excitations within the material hosting the probed optical transition. A distinct form of transient absorption spectroscopy, termed proximity transient absorption (PTA), is demonstrated, in which the probed optical transition and the monitored photoexcited carriers reside in different materials. Using graphene/hBN/WS$_2$ heterostructures, photoexcited carriers in graphene induce a strong transient optical response at the excitonic resonance of a WS$_2$ monolayer through Coulomb screening, even when the two layers remain electronically isolated by an atomically thin hBN spacer.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #optics-photonics #combinatorics

entry.title: Fibres and glasses are competing material states in protein condensation
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03415-z Fibres are thought to emerge from a dense protein condensate ageing into a glassy state. It is now shown that protein fibres and glassy condensates may result from two competing ageing pathways.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics #genomics-proteins

entry.title: Light-induced asymmetric pseudogap below the critical temperature in cuprates
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 20 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03446-6 How superconductivity relates to the pseudogap in cuprates remains unclear. Now, time-resolved photoemission measurements show a light-induced pseudogap-like state below critical temperature, revealing a dynamic interplay with superconductivity.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics #condensed-matter

entry.title: A liquid-crystal analogue of the skyrmion Hall effect
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03379-0 Magnetic skyrmions are known to exhibit a Hall effect in the presence of an electric current. Now it is shown that liquid-crystal solitons also exhibit a Hall-like drift under shear flow.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics

entry.title: Evidence for spin-fluctuation-mediated superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 19 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03454-6 The mechanism for superconductivity in cuprates is still not known. Now, the observation of a relationship between the critical temperature and strength of coupling between electrons and spin fluctuations suggests the latter as a prime candidate.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics #number-theory #condensed-matter

entry.summary:
